summary: Discovery with ACME Bank about air-gapped / on-prem private deployment. Primary concerns: offline updates, hardware constraints (preferred GPUs, NVLink, no internet egress), security/compliance (KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO), and timeline for a pilot. Redwood AE+SE outlined hosted/dedicated/private options, proposed an on-prem pilot and follow-up technical deep dive.
topics: offline model updates and deployment cadence
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-03-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Evan Grant (Redwood CSM), Mark Reynolds (ACME Head of Platform), Sofia Martinez (ACME Security Architect), Dr. Alan Chu (ACME ML Lead), Tanya Lopez (ACME Procurement)
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, AE on the account, we also have Priya our SE and Evan from CS. Quick check, audio ok?
00:10 Mark Reynolds: yep good here, thanks.
00:15 Priya Shah: morning all, excited to dig in.
00:22 Jordan Lee: High level — we understand you have regulated workloads, want an on-prem air-gapped deployment path. Today we want to understand constraints: hardware, update cadence, who's the approvers and success criteria.
00:35 Sofia Martinez: Correct. From security side we need no egress to internet, keys must be in HSM, audit logs exported to our SIEM, and SOC 2/ISO evidence.
00:48 Jordan Lee: Totally understood. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages — in air-gap mode we ship a self-contained bundle. There are a couple of patterns: periodic offline model updates via signed artifacts, or isolated package installs. Either works depending on your change window.
01:05 Dr. Alan Chu: Can you explain how model updates happen offline, like if we want H100s on-prem and we need a 100GB model quantized, what's the workflow?
01:18 Priya Shah: Sure — typical approach is we create a signed model artifact and a validated runtime container. For true air-gap you get an offline bundle on storage media, checksum signed by Redwood, customer runs a verification step using their own KMS/HSM. The runtime supports restarting without egress. Note: we call out checksums and signature verification.
01:38 Mark Reynolds: Who does the signing? Our compliance requires we control keys.
01:42 Priya Shah: You can use your HSM to sign the final step; Redwood can sign upstream and you re-sign internally in your controlled flow. Some customers prefer we provide the image and you re-sign.
01:55 Sofia Martinez: What about telemetry and metrics? We need traces but can't send them out.
02:02 Evan Grant: In Pure air-gap mode telemetry is stored locally and can be exported via secure file transfer to your analytics stack. You can also opt into local-only dashboards; no cloud egress unless you enable it.
02:15 Dr. Alan Chu: Performance — in our last benchmarks we saw issues with KV cache and latency for long-context prompts. Does Redwood runtime support KV cache persistence across restarts in on-prem?
02:28 Priya Shah: Yes, the runtime supports KV cache checkpoints and warmup. In on-prem mode we can configure persistent cache on local NVMe; for large models we recommend 1.5-2x sequence memory overhead, and we profile for A100/H100. Note some kernel optimizations vary by driver level.
02:46 Mark Reynolds: hardware question — we have a mix of A100 80GB and some H100s; do you have requirements for NVLink or Mellanox NICs?
02:55 Priya Shah: Preferred topology: NVLink for multi-GPU model parallelism; for inference serving most customers use NVLink for large offload. Mellanox/ConnectX with RoCE works for RDMA; we provide a compatibility matrix. We'll share the SKUs we validate.
03:10 Jordan Lee: quick note — we'll attach the hardware compatibility matrix. link: https://redwood.example/onprem/hw-matrix.pdf
03:20 Dr. Alan Chu: If we need model quantization, do you manage that or do we?
03:24 Priya Shah: We can provide quantized variants and guidance. For strict air-gap, we can deliver the quantized artifact as part of the offline bundle. We often recommend INT8/4-bit quant based on evals; but we also deliver quality regression tests.
03:40 Sofia Martinez: Encryption at rest and key management — must integrate with our KMS. Can Redwood plug into our Vault/HSM?
03:47 Priya Shah: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS. For on-prem we can integrate with HashiCorp Vault, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault (in hybrid), and HSMs via PKCS#11. We'll map the APIs during the deep dive.
04:05 Mark Reynolds: What about patching the runtime? Security patches are a big concern.
04:10 Evan Grant: For air-gap we provide patch bundles and CVE notices. You can consume them via secure transfer; we also provide guidance to apply patches and a test playbook. If needed Redwood can send a field engineer for the initial rollout under an enterprise support engagement.
04:26 Sofia Martinez: Any automated health checks that call home? We can't have that.
04:30 Priya Shah: Default telemetry is disabled in air-gap. Health checks run locally; we provide a local agent to surface health into your Prometheus stack.
04:38 Jordan Lee: Turning to procurement and timeline — Tanya, do you have any constraints?
04:42 Tanya Lopez: We need the procurement timeline: typical PO process takes 4-6 weeks after SOW, security review might add two weeks. Target for pilot would be late April / early May.
04:54 Jordan Lee: Okay good to know. For the POC we typically propose a 6-week pilot: week 1 infra validation, week 2 model shipping & integration, weeks 3-4 performance validation and tuning, final 1-2 weeks for ops/hardening.
05:12 Dr. Alan Chu: What are success criteria? Latency p95 < 200ms for short prompts and stable throughput of N qps?
05:20 Jordan Lee: Exactly — define target p95 and throughput for your critical endpoints; add quality metrics for generation. We'll agree SLOs in SOW.
05:29 Mark Reynolds: Cost — rough difference between Redwood Dedicated reserved vs on-prem private?
05:33 Jordan Lee: Broadly, Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs in our DC) has predictable monthly commits; on-prem shifts capital to you but reduces per-token usage fees and gives full control. We'll put numbers in an estimate.
05:45 Sofia Martinez: One more security detail: audit logs retention and export format? SIEM needs syslog/JSONL export and signed tamper-evidence.
05:55 Priya Shah: We produce structured audit logs in JSONL and can stream to local syslog or S3-compatible storage. We also support signed log bundles for tamper-evidence.
06:08 Jordan Lee: I'm hearing a few clear blockers: 1) must be fully air-gapped with internal key control, 2) hardware validation for your A100/H100 mix, 3) offline update process validated by security, 4) procurement timeline. We'll follow up with artifacts and a technical deep dive.
06:24 Mark Reynolds: Sounds right. Also want a performance run book and expected CPU/GPU ratios per qps.
06:32 Priya Shah: We'll include runbook snippets and perf tuning knobs — batching, kv cache sizes, sequence length optimizations.
06:40 Dr. Alan Chu: For benchmarking, can you run a synthetic workload against our models or do we need to provide test prompts?
06:46 Jordan Lee: We prefer using your representative prompt sets for real-world metrics; we can run a mixed synthetic if needed. We'll sign an NDA if you want Redwood to handle any PII.
06:56 Sofia Martinez: Regarding legal, we'll need to see data handling clauses for on-prem and a statement about no cloud egress.
07:02 Jordan Lee: Understood, we'll attach a tailored SOW clause.
07:06 Tanya Lopez: Can you share licensing model? If we go on-prem pilot, is there a license fee?
07:10 Jordan Lee: For pilots we typically have a modest pilot fee to cover engineering and support; longer term licensing depends on reserved capacity vs on-prem perpetual with support—will outline in estimate.
07:22 Dr. Alan Chu: One operational question — how do infra upgrades happen? Firmware, drivers?
07:27 Priya Shah: We document driver versions and supported CUDA/driver matrix; upgrades follow your change management window. We'll supply validated container images for each driver set.
07:39 Mark Reynolds: Any known issues with multi-tenancy on the same cluster if we run other workloads?
07:45 Priya Shah: We recommend isolated GPU pools for Redwood inference to avoid noisy neighbors. Our runtime has cgroup isolation and we support tenant-level quotas.
07:58 Jordan Lee: Quick pause — I want to note down next steps. We'll send: security docs (SOC2/ISO), on-prem deployment checklist, hardware matrix, and propose dates for the tech deep dive.
08:10 Sofia Martinez: Do you have reference customers in finance who've done air-gap?
08:15 Jordan Lee: Yes, a few banks and payments companies — we'll provide anonymized references and an excerpted case study.
08:22 Dr. Alan Chu: Any limitations on model size for on-prem?
08:26 Priya Shah: Practically it's bound by GPU memory and NVLink topology; we can support multi-GPU sharding for very large models. We'll include shard recommendations.
08:36 Jordan Lee: Let's call out timelines: we'll aim to send artifacts by Fri 2025-03-06 and schedule deep dive for 2025-03-11. Does that work?
08:44 Mark Reynolds: Works for us.
08:46 Tanya Lopez: Works for procurement.
08:48 Jordan Lee: Great — thank you everyone. We'll follow up with an email and the attachments.
09:00 End of call.

Notes: transcript includes occasional ASR errors (e.g., "Redwood Dedikated" in a few places), filler words removed in spots. Shared artifacts: https://redwood.example/security/soc2-summary.pdf, https://redwood.example/onprem/hw-matrix.pdf, POC checklist spreadsheet (link provided in follow-up).
